📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough fans will be hoping that the 2026/27 season is one which ends in promotion under Kim Hellberg, having spent the best part of a decade outside the Premier League.

To football supporters of a certain era, it would also feel right to see the Teesside outfit competing amongst English football's elite, having spent the majority of the 1990s and 2000s in the top-flight, whilst boasting some top talents during that time.

Such pedigree is what makes potentially signing for Boro such an attractive proposition right now, with Steve Gibson remaining as ambitious as ever, which was demonstrated this summer by the high-profile signing of Will Lankshear.

In his first months at the Riverside Stadium, the highly-rated centre-forward has certainly been the talk of the town, but where does he rank in comparison to the club's best strikers this century? FLW have debated such questions...

Kickstarting this list of Middlesbrough goalscoring supremos is Chuba Akpom, who spent three years at the Riverside.

The former Arsenal academy graduate's first two seasons on Teesside were certainly not ones to write home about, but his exploits in the 2022/23 season will not be forgotten anytime soon.

After netting a brace against Sheffield United under Chris Wilder in August 2022, Akpom ended the campaign as the Championship's top scorer and player of the season after netting 28 goals in 38 appearances, including a run of 14 goals in as many games between February and April 2023.

Such form then paved the way for his £12.2m switch to Ajax, where he also enjoyed relative goalscoring success.

In sixth is Alvaro Negredo, who still left a lasting impression on Middlesbrough fans regardless of their side's relegation during his only season at the club.

The Spanish forward won the Premier League with Manchester City just three seasons before he was loaned in from Valencia, and his top-level experience was made clear for all to see at the Riverside.

Including a debut strike against Stoke City, Negredo scored nine times and provided four assists in just 36 Premier League appearances, before winding down his professional career in Turkey, Saudi Arabia and his native Spain.

Lankshear is up next, with the England youth international already earning rave reviews on Teesside.

There were question marks over Tottenham Hotspur's decision to accept an initial £10m deal, which could rise to £20m depending on add-ons, and the 21-year-old is only adding to those on a weekly basis.

The forward, unsurprisingly, leads the way as the Championship's top scorer this season, which is largely down to a remarkable run of 13 goals in as many games prior to a minor injury, which derailed his chances of becoming the first second-tier player in 14 years to have received a call-up to the senior Three Lions squad.

Alen Boksic was 30 years old by the time he arrived in the North East from Lazio for £2.5m, but it certainly proved to be a bargain deal.

The 40-time Croatian international had already scored 34 goals in Serie A for the Rome outfit and Juventus, and in his first campaign at the Riverside, netted 12 times and was named Middlesbrough's Player of the Season.

It begs the question as to how many goals he could have gone on to score in the Premier League for the Reds, as, in February 2003, Boksic made the decision to retire after injury issues, with his top-flight record reading 22 goals in just 68 appearances.

In third place is Yakubu, with the Nigerian proving to be an inspired £7.5m buy from Portsmouth in 2005.

The 2005/06 campaign is one remembered with great fondness by Middlesbrough supporters, as Steve McClaren's side reached the UEFA Cup final, despite eventually losing to Sevilla.

The Nigerian striker scored 19 times in all competitions throughout said campaign, including a crucial winner against Roma in March 2006, before hitting double-figures the following season despite the club's second successive mid-table finish.

Ultimately, 35 goals and 11 assists in 104 appearances allowed Boro to make a profit, as Yakubu signed for Everton in an £11.25m deal.

Which of these Middlesbrough strikers has been your favourite to watch? Comment below!

Jimmy Floyd-Hasselbaink's quality at the top level was also clear to see by the time he arrived at Middlesbrough in the summer of 2004, with the club competing in the UEFA Cup that particular campaign also, having defeated Bolton Wanderers in the EFL Cup final the season previous.

The Dutchman had previously scored over 150 times for the likes of Atlético Madrid, Leeds United and Chelsea, and in his first season at the Riverside, hit 16 goals and provided nine assists across 57 games in all competitions, including the vital strike against Manchester City which, again, guaranteed European qualification.

Hasselbaink still had a strong influence in his second and final season for the Reds too, scoring 17 times in all competitions, including four in the UEFA Cup, with the final defeat to Sevilla being the last of his 89 appearances.

Mark Viduka had already certified himself as a lethal finisher with the likes of Dinamo Zagreb, Celtic and Leeds United, with Middlesbrough fans also getting three seasons' worth of joy out of the Australian international after his Elland Road exit.

After a disappointing first campaign at the Riverside, Viduka then hit double figures in both of his remaining two seasons, with seven of his 16 strikes across 2005/06 helping McClaren's side to Eindhoven - three of which came in the dramatic quarter-final and semi-final comebacks over FC Basel and Steaua Bucharest.

In 2006/07, Viduka netted 14 Premier League goals, including a run of five goals in the final four games of the campaign, as well as five goals in seven FA Cup appearances, before he eventually moved to North East rivals, Newcastle United, upon the expiration of his contract.

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

In a recent development, only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, released a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

In a recent development, it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Sources indicate that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Sources indicate that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a substantial mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

According to recent reports, “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

It has been revealed that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Industry observers note that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

In a recent development, there has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
  • In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Recent findings suggest that extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Istanbul Governor's Office remarked 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive.

It has been revealed that reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Recent findings suggest that gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

In a recent development, yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'.

In a recent development, galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'.

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray.

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

It has been revealed that villa defender Ian Maatsen mentioned: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

According to recent reports, galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’.

In a recent development, villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Industry observers note that repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

In a recent development, when the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

According to recent reports, what next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

Recent findings suggest that to invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

According to recent reports, there were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet rapidly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

It has been revealed that elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United are struggling in the Championship right now, and whilst Scott Parker will be aiming to turn things around swiftly in West London, the former Burnley boss may have one eye on the January window already.

It hasn't been the start to life Parker hoped for at West Ham when he succeeded Nuno Espírito Santo in early November, failing to win any of his first four games in charge against Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End, and Portsmouth.

With three promotions from the Championship as a manager on his CV, the former England and Hammers midfielder will certainly be backing himself to turn these fortunes around sooner rather than later, but red flags are everywhere around the London Stadium right now.

Parker will be looking to stamp his authority on the West Ham squad in the January window, but first, he must make sure he is still in charge by then, as his intentions for where he wants to improve have been revealed.

As revealed by Alan Nixon via Patreon in mid-November, Parker is looking to target key positions in his West Ham squad ahead of the January window - namely centre-forward and left-back.

Neither Taty Castellanos nor Pablo Felipe have adapted particularly well to the Championship since relegation, leaving just Joel Piroe as his main focal point up top as things stand.

Meanwhile, Ezra Mayers has emerged as his preferred option at left-back right now over the likes of Ollie Scarles, Adama Boiro, and Morato, with the 19-year-old being thrown straight into the deep end by Parker.

With the number of goals the Hammers are scoring having dipped in recent weeks, a new centre-forward being on the cards isn't a surprise, as one standout candidate ought to be on the cards.

Blackburn Rovers striker Andri Gudjohnsen will be a name that begins to dominate headlines as we approach the January transfer window, with the Icelandic striker having caught fire at Ewood Park this campaign.

With 11 goals and one assist in 16 Championship games this season, the 24-year-old has exploded into life in Lancashire, and alongside Will Lankshear, has emerged as the standout centre-forward in the division.

Gudjohnsen, according to FotMob, has an expected goal return of just 4.43 this campaign from 25 shots, scoring with nearly every other shot he takes and overperforming wildly in front of goal, displaying elite finishing ability.

The centre-forward will be on the list of numerous clubs across the United Kingdom and the rest of Europe heading into winter, but aside from being a deadly finisher, Parker has one more clear reason to win the race for his signature.

Parker has established himself as one of the most successful managers in Championship history over the years, having earned promotion with each of Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley.

With the Clarets, Parker reached a century of points during the 2024/25 campaign, only being pipped to the league title by Leeds United on goal difference, conceding a record-low of 16 goals across the entire season.

Although he was unable to keep Burnley in the top flight last year, he remains a well-regarded boss at Turf Moor, and his connection to the club would certainly annoy Blackburn supporters if he were to sign Gudjohnsen.

Blackburn will be expecting substantial offers for their star man this winter, as supporters will be hoping that he doesn't head to the Hammers amid this obvious connection.

In a recent development, how much do you think Andri Gudjohnsen would cost this winter? Where do you think he should go? Share your thoughts below!

Interest in Gudjohnsen this winter is inevitable, as Blackburn will face a massive battle to keep the Icelandic international at Ewood Park for the remainder of the season.

Whether any submitted bids will prove to be enough to lure him away from the club remains to be seen, as Blackburn supporters hope one of those doesn't arrive from the Hammers.

West Ham, given their current predicament in the Championship, will face a tougher task than they're used to in convincing the striker to join them, as they will have to register their interest in Gudjohnsen ASAP to have any sort of chance of obtaining his services.

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 19:11.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has confirmed Junior Kroupi has been reinstated to the Europa League squad ahead of Thursday’s clash against Celta Vigo.

The France international was initially named in the Europa League squad despite undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

However, Kroupi’s absence allowed Bournemouth to use UEFA’s temporary injury replacement rule to include Ben Gannon-Doak for the first four games in the league phase.

Kroupi returned to action last month, but as a result of Gannon-Doak’s inclusion in the Europa League squad, he was unable to feature in the 3-1 win over Sparta Prague at the start of the month.

Rose has now confirmed Kroupi has been brought back into the Europa League squad, meaning Gannon-Doak will drop out for the final four league phase matches unless there are any further injury replacement opportunities.

Alex Scott is also available to make his first Europa League appearance since matchday one after returning from a thigh injury with a substitute appearance in Saturday’s 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

"Everyone is ready,” Rose said. "We have no newly introduced injuries ahead of tomorrow's game.

“We are glad to have Alex and Junior back and available.".

In a recent development, when asked whether the pair will start in Vigo, Rose remarked: "It could be possible, but also maybe not. We will see".

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are without the injured trio of Julian Araujo, Juanlu Sanchez and Alex Toth.

Bournemouth are currently enjoying the longest winning run in the club's history after recording a ninth consecutive victory in all competitions at the weekend.

They also boast a perfect record in their maiden European campaign, having won their four league phase matches by a combined 11-2 scoreline.

As a result, they head into matchday five in second spot in the Europa League league phase and five points clear of the teams sitting just outside the top eight.

Gordon has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Barcelona have now picked up 12 points from their five matches in the league stage of the Champions League, which has left them in fourth spot in the overall table.

Flick's team were missing Lamine Yamal on Wednesday due to a slight ankle injury; in his absence, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus were also on the scoresheet.

Barcelona will be aiming to make it six straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan outfit will then welcome Atletico Madrid to Camp Nou in their first match of December, before facing Celta Vigo in their third league game in quick succession.

Barcelona's next Champions League game is at home to Manchester City on December 8.

#141342. The last 7 permanent Lincoln City managers ranked from worst to best

The last 7 permanent Lincoln City managers ranked from worst to best

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There arguably isn't a better run club in the EFL right now than Lincoln City.
  • It has been revealed that the Imps were a National League side just a decade ago, and presently find themselves in the second tier for the first time since the 1960/61 campaign.
  • In a footballing landscape where managers are axed off the back of one bad season, or a poor run of form, it's impressive that a list like this, detailing who has been the best manager (or managers) at Sincil Bank out of the last seven hires, stretches back all the way to 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There arguably isn't a better run club in the EFL right now than Lincoln City.

It has been revealed that the Imps were a National League side just a decade ago, and presently find themselves in the second tier for the first time since the 1960/61 campaign. That's been achieved thanks to sustainability off the pitch and patience on it.

In a footballing landscape where managers are axed off the back of one bad season, or a poor run of form, it's impressive that a list like this, detailing who has been the best manager (or managers) at Sincil Bank out of the last seven hires, stretches back all the way to 2013.

Since their promotion back to the EFL in 2017, only four managers were needed to get to where they are now. That's a good sign, but which of the last seven main dugout men have been the best?

Football League World has taken a look to find out.

Back in 2013, Lincoln weren't the remarkable football club that many know them to be. Instead, they were treading water in the National League, after being relegated from League Two a couple of years earlier.

The seventh-most recent Lincoln boss takes seventh spot, as Gary Simpson didn't do too much while in charge at Sincil Bank.

The former midfielder returned to Lincolnshire a decade after spending five months as caretaker boss during their time in the old Division Three (now League Two), with the club sitting two places and two points above the drop zone in the fifth tier.

He did enough to stave off relegation, but did need back-to-back wins in their final two games against Tamworth and Hyde United to make fully sure.

Simpson then oversaw a 14th-placed finish in the 2013/14 campaign before being placed on gardening leave and later sacked months into 2014/15.

Chris Moyses was the man to replace Gary Simpson, initially as caretaker when the latter was placed on gardening leave, and then permanently a month later after two wins and a draw in his first three league games.

Things started okay, with six wins in seven games to close out 2014, but the rest of the season was nothing more than mediocre, with the Imps finishing 15th.

He'd be given the 2015/16 campaign, and despite an okay start with Lincoln sitting around the top eight by the upcoming year, it ended with another drab finish and a 13th-placed position, which was actually their best in the five years they'd been at the level.

Fast forward six years, and Lincoln were now pretty well-established in League One thanks to the good work of some people who we'll get to soon enough.

The Imps made the third-tier play-offs in 2021, but the following season finished 12 places and 25 points worse off in 17th. In came former Liverpool, Manchester City and Wolves left-sider Mark Kennedy, who had spent the last year as Lee Bowyer's assistant at Birmingham City.

He was given a four-year contract, which wouldn't have been seen as strange at the time, given his two predecessors lasted three seasons each, but Kennedy wasn't really able to push the club forward.

The Irishman oversaw a better season than the one previous in 2022/23, finishing 11th in League One and leading Lincoln to the fourth round of the EFL Cup, their best run in the competition in 55 years.

But despite only losing one of their first nine games in all competitions the following season, a run of poor results saw him sacked in October, a little over a year into that four-year deal.

It's hard to properly rank the current managerial duo at Lincoln, given they've only held the post for half a year, and they've been the men tasked with keeping the Imps competitive at their highest level for over 60 years.

Sources indicate that so far, though, they're not doing a terrible job. The Imps started well, taking Middlesbrough all the way to the end on opening day in defeat, beating the likes of Bolton Wanderers and Bristol City away and destroying Burnley at Sincil Bank.

Their form has slipped, though, and now they're looking over their shoulders at the drop zone, which many critics expected them to do anyway.

The higher-ups at Sincil Bank have the faith that they can turn things around, and for now, they rank slap bang in the middle of this list.

Michael Appleton had big shoes to fill in the Lincoln dugout when he replaced Danny Cowley just weeks into the 2019/20 campaign, after the fan favourite departed for Huddersfield Town.

It was the Imps' first year at third tier-level since a brief campaign in the old Division Two in the 1998/99 season, and, as has become the case now in the Championship, many expected their backs to be against the wall.

Despite not winning in his first five games in all competitions, which included a 6-0 home defeat against Oxford United and a loss against Manchester United's kids in the EFL Trophy, he managed to keep the Imps competitive, and when the league was curtailed due to COVID, Lincoln were 16th on PPG.

Appleton's best season came the following year, though, when an Imps side bolstered by the likes of Morgan Rogers and Brennan Johnson alongside the more experienced heads of Jorge Grant and Anthony Scully led the club to a fifth-placed finish.

They beat Sunderland over two legs in the semi-final and took the lead against Blackpool at Wembley, but ended up losing the final 2-1 thanks to a Kenny Dougall double.

Unfortunately, they didn't recover from that hangover and finished 17th the following season. Appleton departed at the end of that term, after a real rollercoaster three years at the club.

The hiring of Michael Skubala raised some eyebrows at the time. The former England futsal coach and Leeds United Under-21s boss had never managed at senior level in the football pyramid, barring a three-game caretaker spell at Elland Road after the dismissal of Marcelo Bielsa.

However, Skubala's time at Sincil Bank was incredible. Replacing Mark Kennedy in November 2023, Lincoln became an established play-off contender under him, until they exploded into life last season and won the division with 103 points.

Industry observers note that back at the start, though, questions were being asked after a four-game losing run over the Christmas period in 2023. Skubala's side followed that up with a 16-game unbeaten run, which included consecutive wins by a 1-5, 6-0 and 5-0 scoreline to be right amongst the play-offs talk.

In the end, they gave themselves too much to do and finished seventh. A similar Christmas run the following year couldn't be saved, and they finished 11th.

Industry observers note that last season doesn't need to be dressed up, though. Lincoln were brilliant, especially in the second half of the campaign. They went 29 games unbeaten, a club record, and earned 12 more points than anyone else in 2026.

Unfortunately, Skubala opted not to take his Imps side into the second tier, instead leaving for Bristol City, a decision which isn't looking to be the right one.

There arguably isn't a better modern-day manager at Sincil Bank than Danny Cowley, though, who oversaw two promotions, an EFL Trophy win and a miraculous FA Cup run in just three years at the helm.

Industry observers note that let's head all the way back to 2016, when Lincoln had just parted ways with Chris Moyses after just under two years in charge. The Imps finished 13th, which backed up 15th, 14th, 16th and 17th-placed finishes in the National League.

It has been revealed that is Danny Cowley the best manager Lincoln City have had out of the last seven? Let us know what you think in the comments.

Industry observers note that in Cowley's first year in charge, Lincoln won the fifth tier, while also making it to the quarter-final of the FA Cup in one of the most memorable runs in recent history. The Imps beat Championship sides Ipswich Town and Brighton, as well as Premier League outfit Burnley, before losing to Arsenal.

Their first season back in the EFL for seven years saw them immediately finish in the play-offs, while also juggling a run to the final of the EFL Trophy, which they won, beating Shrewsbury Town to become the first fourth-tier side in nine years to lift the trophy.

Then, the following year they won League Two, making it three pieces of silverware in three years under Cowley and a return to the third tier for the first time since before the millennium.

Lincoln's rise up the EFL began with Cowley, and those who have been in the stands at Sincil Bank since their time in the National League still reminisce about how legendary his time at the club was.

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

Sources indicate that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

It has been revealed that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It has been revealed that it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson stated, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

In a recent development, “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola remarked. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Industry observers note that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Sources indicate that cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

It has been revealed that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose remarked. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola stated: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. Sources indicate that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

According to recent reports, his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Recent findings suggest that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He noted: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

In a recent development, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Recent findings suggest that liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Industry observers note that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.
  • Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that the decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders presently benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he noted when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk.".

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

Industry observers note that "Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us.".

Those comments underline the advantages presently enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly important in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho said. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half.".

It has been revealed that his explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

Militao faces a different challenge.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive plans.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not unveiled prepares to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen presently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship promotion race is on, and though there is still plenty of the season remaining for numerous twists and turns to occur, three standout candidates have emerged.

Just ticking over a third of the way through the 2026/27 Championship season, there is almost nothing to separate the teams at the top of the table right now, as one good or bad game week can see a side fly up or down the table.

Unlike in previous years, where the likes of Coventry City, Burnley, and Norwich City have romped their way to the second tier titles, there appears to be no standout side this time around, with the quality of the division as a whole at an all-time high.

Out of the 24 teams, only three will earn a spot in what is widely regarded as Europe's most coveted division, as three teams have put their names in the hat as some of the favourites.

Heading into gameweek 17 of the Championship, Middlesbrough, Stoke City, and Birmingham City made up the top three in that order, with the Potters having claimed a crucial win over Blues the previous weekend.

Boro enjoyed an excellent transfer window over the summer, guided by head coach Kim Hellberg as the likes of Will Lankshear, Sebastian Berhalter, Ashley Phillips, and Radek Vitek have demonstrated why they were worth the money.

Stoke, despite losing each of their three opening league games, have bounced back with ten wins, two draws, and one defeat in their following 13 games to emerge as surprise contenders under Mark Robins.

Chris Davies is looking to continue Birmingham's rise up the divisions by becoming increasingly watertight at the back and efficient up top, as the Blues look to end their near 16-year absence from the Premier League.

Certainly, the likes of Wolverhampton Wanderers, West Bromwich Albion, Southampton, Queens Park Rangers, Swansea City, Sheffield United, Portsmouth, Norwich City, and West Ham United, each of whom are just a matter of points away, will have something to say about the promotion race come May.

There is a reason that teams in the Championship spend so much money in the hope that they can be playing Premier League football the following season, as with success comes a huge boost in finances.

According to Sports Illustrated, promotion to the English top flight is worth in excess of £200 million in prize money alone, and that goes for first-place, second-place, and the play-off winner.

The Championship play-off final is widely regarded as the richest game in club football for a reason, as essentially two teams go head-to-head in a one-off final for a straight shootout for promotion, with the winner taking it all.

With the second-tier play-off system expanding from four teams to six this year, there are more places up for grabs than ever to earn a place under the Wembley arch at the end of the season.

A nine-figure cash prize is on offer for the three teams who are able to go all the way, though who they will be remains to be seen.

Industry observers note that who do you think will be promoted this season and earn this eye-watering cash prize? Do you think your team will go up? Share your thoughts below!

Though each of Stoke, Birmingham, and Middlesbrough has had terrific starts to the season, whether they can all maintain their level of form throughout the campaign remains to be seen.

Stoke started hot last campaign before dropping off in the second half of the year. Birmingham persistently flirted with the top six but couldn't quite break in, and Boro fell at the final hurdle to Hull City after missing out on automatic promotion.

With so many teams clustered around the top half right now, the promotion battle has never been hotter, as Stoke, Birmingham, and Middlesbrough don't face a straightforward route to the Premier League.

The best combined Southampton & Middlesbrough XI right now - Jack Stephens axed

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Middlesbrough travel to St Mary's to take on automatic promotion rivals Southampton on Friday night, with the two clubs meeting for the first time since the now-infamous 'spygate' scandal, in what is shaping up to be a feisty affair.
  • As things stand, Middlesbrough sit top of the Championship table, level on points with Stoke City but with a superior goal difference, as Kim Hellberg's side look to extend their lead at the top of the division when they travel to Southampton on Friday night.
  • This will be the first time the two clubs have met since the 'spygate' scandal took place, with the Saints being expelled from the play-offs despite beating Boro over two legs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough travel to St Mary's to take on automatic promotion rivals Southampton on Friday night, with the two clubs meeting for the first time since the now-infamous 'spygate' scandal, in what is shaping up to be a feisty affair.

As things stand, Middlesbrough sit top of the Championship table, level on points with Stoke City but with a superior goal difference, as Kim Hellberg's side look to extend their lead at the top of the division when they travel to Southampton on Friday night.

This will be the first time the two clubs have met since the 'spygate' scandal took place, with the Saints being expelled from the play-offs despite beating Boro over two legs.

Although that occurred some six months ago, it will still be fresh in the memories of not only both sets of supporters, but of players and coaches alike, and with both teams targeting automatic promotion this year, tensions will be high.

Both sides can boast some exceptional talent across the board, as Football League World takes a closer look at the two teams and attempts to create an overall best XI from these two Championship behemoths.

For the purpose of this XI, a 4-2-3-1 shape will be used, with both sides having often deployed that formation this campaign.

In between the sticks, our pick is Southampton's Daniel Peretz, just about pipping Radek Vitek to a place in the side.

Peretz joined the Saints in January 2026, initially on loan from Bayern Munich, as Eckert looked to replace Gavin Bazunu in goal with a safe pair of hands, and with the 26-year-old, he certainly succeeded.

According to FotMob, the Israeli international prevented 6.54 goals during the second half of last season, among the very best records in the Championship despite a lack of minutes in comparison to the other keepers.

Unsurprisingly, Southampton would make the move permanent in the summer for just £6.05 million, and he has continued to impress on the South Coast with his displays, taking his place as our number one.

Beginning our back four at right-back is Middlesbrough's Callum Brittain, with the 28-year-old our pick as the first defender just ahead of James Bree.

Bree was recalled from his loan at Charlton Athletic by Southampton in January 2026 as one of Eckert's first major decisions at the helm, and since then, he has been an almost ever-present in the side.

However, Brittain gets the nod in this XI, being equally as vital for Hellberg on Teesside ever since his move from Blackburn Rovers in the summer of 2025, barely missing a game and captaining the side on occasion.

In his prime years, Brittain is among the best and most underrated full-backs the Championship has to offer, and whilst a solid argument for Bree's inclusion over him could be made, it's the Boro man who gets the nod for us.

Adilson Malanda agreed to join Middlesbrough in the summer of 2025 from MLS side Charlotte, having emerged as one of the best defenders in North America, but wouldn't officially make the move to Teesside until the following January.

The Frenchman, since his arrival, has been a constant in Hellberg's side, with his calm nature and technical ability a standout feature of his game, allowing him to move into midfield if required.

An excellent one-on-one defender as well, the 25-year-old has proven to be an excellent pickup from Boro, and whilst Ashley Phillips and Luke Ayling will put forward arguments to be included in this side, Malanda's inclusion was never really up for debate.

German defender Keven Schlotterbeck joined Southampton in the summer, essentially replacing the outgoing Taylor Harwood-Bellis, who joined Aston Villa for around £30 million.

Signed from Augsburg for around a tenth (£3 million) of what they sold Harwood-Bellis for, Southampton's defence hasn't gotten any worse since the introduction of the 29-year-old, and some may argue it has actually improved.

The brother of Borussia Dortmund and German international Nico Schlotterbeck, Keven has forged an excellent career for himself, with over 150 Bundesliga appearances, and now has taken his talents to St Mary's, where he has emerged as one of the best centre-backs in the division this season.

Jack Stephens, Nathan Wood, and Zach Abbott may feel as though they have arguments to be involved, though our pick for this spot is Schlotterbeck.

Completing the back line is another Southampton player in the form of Ryan Manning, with the Irishman having established himself as one of the best full-backs in the division over the past few years.

The 30-year-old first made the move to England with Queens Park Rangers in January 2015, and across spells with the R's, Rotherham United, Swansea City, and now Southampton, is approaching 300 Championship appearances; he could make his 300th appearance in the division against Middlesbrough.

Like Bree, Manning has been a constant in the Saints side since the German's appointment in late 2025, and has proven to be excellent both going forwards and in defence, take his place in this side.

Neto Borges and Max Arfsten can make claims, though our pick to complete the back four is the Irishman.

Beginning our midfield pairing is USMNT international Aidan Morris, who, over the past few years, has quietly become one of, if not the best midfielders in the entire Championship.

Joining Middlesbrough from MLS side Columbus Crew in the summer of 2024 for around $4 million (£3.14 million), the 25-year-old was often out of the limelight at the expense of midfield partner Hayden Hackney, but following Hackney's departure to Everton in the recent window, he has taken the mantle.

When fit, Morris is one of the first names on the Middlesbrough team sheet, with his presence in the middle of the park almost irreplaceable for the Swedish head coach, capable of breaking up play, dictating tempo, and, more recently, becoming more of a goal threat.

Bundesliga side Stuttgart have reportedly registered an interest in recent weeks, though Boro will have no intention of parting ways with Morris anytime soon, especially with Premier League football on the line.

Joining Morris in the midfield is current teammate and compatriot Sebastian Berhalter, who, having made the move to England in the summer, has adapted seamlessly to the Championship and looks a cut above.

Capped 24 times by the USA men's national team, appearing at the World Cup and scoring, Berhalter has replaced Hackney in Middlesbrough's midfield with ease, and if Boro are to achieve any sort of success this year, he will almost certainly be pivotal to those efforts.

A midfield duo of Morris and Berhalter will be argued by Saints supporters, who will believe the likes of Caspar Jander, Flynn Downes, and James Ward-Prowse deserve a spot, but we believe the Boro duo just about edge it here.

A player both sides will know well, Irish attacking midfielder Finn Azaz began his career with West Bromwich Albion, but having failed to make a single senior appearance for the Baggies, he made a name for himself through spells with Cheltenham Town, Newport County, Plymouth Argyle, Middlesbrough, and now Southampton.

With Boro, Azaz scored 17 and assisted 17 in 68 games across all competitions for the club, averaging nearly a direct goal contribution every other game before joining Southampton in the summer of 2025 for around £14 million.

Azaz has continued his consistently excellent output at St Mary's, with 14 goals and 16 assists in 66 games across all competitions for Southampton so far, and when his old side travel to the South Coast on Friday, he will be eager to get one over his former employers.

Amario Cozier-Duberry was heavily courted by almost every Championship club over the summer, but it would be Middlesbrough who would sign him on loan from Brighton and Hove Albion in the end.

The 21-year-old came through the youth ranks of Arsenal before joining Brighton in the summer of 2024, and after a quiet loan spell with Blackburn Rovers in 2024/25, shone on loan with Bolton Wanderers in League One last time around.

With the Trotters, Cozier-Duberry scored eight and assisted 12 in 34 third-tier appearances, helping to fire the club back to the Championship, and in 12 league games so far this season, has three goals and six assists.

Best deployed off the right, neither Tom Fellows nor Kuryu Matsuki can make a solid argument for getting ahead of the England youth international in this side.

Brazilian winger Leo Scienza hasn't quite had the best start to this campaign, but his performances from last time around are still fresh in the memory, and one would be brave to deny his undoubted ability.

The 28-year-old joined the Saints in the summer of 2025 from German outfit Heidenheim, having worked his way up to the professional game across spells in the lower reaches of Brazil, Uruguay, Sweden, and Germany.

With seven goals and ten assists in 37 Championship appearances last season, Scienza was pivotal to the Saints' push towards the play-offs, and whilst he hasn't quite yet hit those similar heights this year, he remains a key figure in Eckert's side.

Neither Jeremy Sarmiento nor Tommy Conway get in ahead of the 28-year-old, who takes his place in the final third behind one other player.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

According to recent reports, diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Industry observers note that forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

It has been revealed that few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

In a recent development, with a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Recent findings suggest that juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

According to recent reports, liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the upcoming head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

It has been revealed that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

The Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

It has been revealed that dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

Recent findings suggest that the defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical initiative was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

According to recent reports, united return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the issues exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

Industry observers note that for Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.
